name: Umbilical Cord Ulceration-Intestinal Atresia Syndrome
aliases: Umbilical Cord Ulceration with Intestinal Atresia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Umbilical Cord Ulceration-Intestinal Atresia Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of congenital intestinal atresia confirmed by imaging or surgery
Histopathological evidence of ulceration in the umbilical cord
Evidence of fetal intrauterine hemorrhage or anemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Both major criteria (intestinal atresia and umbilical cord ulceration) must be present; supportive criteria aid confirmation.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often made postnatally or at autopsy due to rarity and severity.

laboratory: Anemia on fetal or neonatal blood testing
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing polyhydramnios and intestinal atresia
Postnatal abdominal X-ray showing intestinal obstruction
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathological confirmation of umbilical cord ulceration

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated intestinal atresia without intrauterine hemorrhage
Umbilical cord insertion abnormality without ulceration

redFlags: Signs of fetal distress during labor
references: Nishijima E et al. Umbilical cord ulceration associated with intestinal atresia: a clinicopathologic study. Pediatr Dev Pathol. 2003.
Orphanet: Umbilical cord ulceration-intestinal atresia syndrome. ORPHA:3405.
Kobayashi H et al. Umbilical cord ulceration and fetal hemorrhage in intestinal atresia. J Obstet Gynaecol Res. 2010.
